questions.q: Why isn't print() enough for a script expected to run unattended for months?
options: print() statements run slower than logging calls
Python limits print() to a maximum of 10 calls per script
print() is not valid Python syntax inside a function
A print statement disappears the moment the terminal closes — nothing records whether an unattended run succeeded, failed, or even ran at all
questions.explain: Without a persistent log, there's no way to answer "did last night's run actually work" after the terminal session is gone.

options: Where and how the script's log messages get written, including a real timestamp and severity level for each entry
A connection pool for multiple simultaneous Snowflake connections
A Snowflake warehouse named ingestion.log
A scheduled task that runs automatically every hour
questions.explain: basicConfig configures the log file, severity threshold, and message format — the foundation for a real, persistent run history.

questions.q: Why does the script catch the exception, log it with logging.error, and then re-raise it rather than swallowing it silently?
options: To prevent the log file from growing too large
Re-raising is required Python syntax and has no real purpose
Because logging.error automatically fixes the underlying problem
So the script still exits with a nonzero status that a scheduler can detect, while also leaving a real record of what went wrong in the log
questions.explain: Logging the error AND re-raising it means both a human reading the log and an automated scheduler checking exit status can detect the failure.

questions.q: What real governance gap from Lesson 1 does a scheduled, logged ingestion script directly close?
options: "Nobody outside the data team can tell what any of this does"
"A bad change ships straight to the dashboard"
"A new raw source gets loaded by hand, when someone remembers"
"Anyone with a password can query or break anything"
questions.explain: A scheduled script with real logging replaces manual, memory-dependent loading with an automatic, auditable process.

questions.q: What is the real job both Windows Task Scheduler and a crontab entry accomplish in this lesson?
options: They both generate the dbt documentation site
They both clean the CSV data before it's loaded
They both run the ingestion script on a fixed recurring schedule, with no human needing to remember to trigger it
They both create the Snowflake warehouse used by the script
questions.explain: Both are real OS-level scheduling mechanisms accomplishing the same job: running the script automatically on a fixed cadence.
